notes.text: Stood — Upon a scaffold set up for him in the court of the people, 2 Chron. vi, 13.
Hast kept — That branch of thy promise concerning the building of this house by David's son.
Keep — Make good the other branch of thy promise.

But will — Is it possible that the great, and high, and lofty God should stoop so low, as to take up his dwelling amongst men? The heaven - All this vast space of the visible heaven. And heaven, &c. - The third and highest, and therefore the largest heaven, called the heaven of heavens for its eminency and comprehensiveness. Contain - For thy essence reacheth far beyond them, being omnipresent. Much less - This house therefore was not built as if it were proportionable to thy greatness, or could contain thee, but only that therein we might serve and glorify thee.
Yet — Tho' thou art not comprehended within this place, yet shew thyself to be graciously present here, by accepting and granting my present requests here tendered unto thee.

Open — To behold with an eye of favour. My name - My presence, and glory and grace. This place - This temple, to which Solomon did now look, and towards which, the godly Israelites directed their looks in their prayers.

In heaven — Which he adds to direct them in their addresses to God in this temple, to lift up their eyes above it, even to heaven, where God's most true, and most glorious dwelling-place is. Forgive - The sins of thy people, praying, and even of their prayers; which, if not pardoned, will certainly hinder the success of all their prayers, and the course of all thy blessings.

They-That constantly abide in thy house; the priests and Levites, or other devout Jews who were there perpetually, as Anna, Luke ii, 36-37. They will — They are continually employed in that blessed work.
Whose strength — Who trusteth in thee as his only strength. Thy ways - Blessed are they whose hearts are set upon Zion and their journey is thither.

Baca — A dry valley in the way to Jerusalem, here put for all places of like nature. Make a well - They dig divers little pits or wells in it for their relief. The rain - God recompenses their diligence with his blessing, sending rain wherewith they may be filled.
They go — They grow stronger and stronger. Appeareth - This is added as the blessed fruit of their long and tedious journey.
Look — Cast a favourable eye towards him. Anointed - Of me, who though a vile sinner, am thine anointed king.
Than dwell — In the greatest glory and plenty.

A sun — To enlighten and quicken, and direct and comfort his people. Shield - To save his people from all their enemies. Grace - His favour, which is better than life. Glory - The honour which comes from God here, and eternal glory. A recital of past, and prayer for present mercy, ver. 1-7. A prediction of a favourable answer, ver. 8-13. To the chief musician, A psalm for the sons of Korah.

glossa.text: *How lovely.* Behold how great the warfare. *For the sparrow,* how secure.

*For the sparrow,* etc. ((AUG.)) To two he renders two: *the heart* as *the sparrow; the flesh* as *the turtle,* to which he gives also *young ones:* with the heart we think upon God, as the sparrow flies to the house; with the flesh we do works. ((CASS.)) As the sparrow forsakes the woods, and rejoices when a house is found, where it fears no snares: so the soul rejoices, while it knows that a house is prepared for it in heaven. The spirit, which is as a sparrow flying on high, reaching towards God himself. *A nest, etc.* ((AUG.)) *A nest* for a time, *a house* true unto eternity. By the nest therefore he means faith, and the conformity of the sacraments of the Church, which nest the turtle seeks, that she may lay up her young. For she does not cast them anywhere, but in the nest of the Church she does good works wholesomely, for which she is saved: wherein she differs from others who do works, but not in the nest of faith. For the pagans also do works, they clothe the naked, etc., and heretics do many things: but not in the nest of the Church, and therefore they are trodden down, they are not preserved. This flesh is the woman, by whom the sparrow is seduced, but she shall be saved by the bearing of works, if in the nest, that is, if she shall have persevered in faith. But God supplies that whereof the nest may be made, for he clothed himself with the hay of the flesh that he might come to thee. *Thy altars, O Lord.* ((CASS.)) Where souls feast at the heavenly banquet, where the soul may rejoice as in a house. ((AUG.)) And the flesh lays up its works, whence: Blessed are they who, etc., where he shows to what beatitude the warfare leads.

*Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord; for ever and ever they shall praise thee.* ((AUG.)) This the good have already, namely, that they dwell in thy house. There follows: *For ever and ever they shall praise thee.* This is the whole business of the saints there: there is no necessity there, which is the mother of all human actions, for whom do they do anything there, where none are in need; they have therefore and they act, whence they are blessed. But every blessed one is called blessed by having or by acting.
*Blessed is the man whose help is from thee: he hath disposed ascensions in his heart.* ((CASS.)) By what help one may come to the house.

*In the vale of tears.* ((CASS.)) The vale of tears is the humility of one repenting. ((AUG.)) But whence the weeping: because he afflicted us with the law, through which we knew that sin fights against the spirit, and we groan, namely how we may come to the place which he has appointed, by his power and help assuredly. *In the place which he hath appointed. For he shall give a blessing.* Which cannot be set forth, which eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, that is, the kingdom to come, which God has disposed and ordained, that it may be come to by degrees.
*O Lord God of hosts.* ((CASS.)) He prays and humbles himself for the obtaining of this help. *God of Jacob.* ((AUG.)) Whom thou madest Israel by appearing to him, so make me also Israel.

*Look upon the face,* etc. For he himself speaks in us, whence the Apostle: *Do you seek a proof of him that speaketh in me, Christ!* And he is received in us, as he says, *He that receiveth you, receiveth me. Look.* The Father always looks upon Christ. ((CASS.)) But make him to be looked upon by the nations *ventibus* through the presence of the incarnation: or, thus by the face we become known to others. ((AUG.)) *Look* therefore *upon the face,* that is, make Christ known to all, that we may be able to go from virtue to virtue

*One day.* Unchangeable, namely without rising and setting, to which yesterday does not yield, which tomorrow does not press upon. *Above thousands,* above the infinite present days, which have an end. For which cause *I have chosen,* though I might reign, *to be abject* in the opinion of men, *in the house,* in the Church, *Behold how sweet it is, to be pressed by the burden of the winepress.*

*Because mercy.* ((CASS.)) Therefore I had rather be in the house of God than elsewhere, because in it he gives mercy, by which he justifies, after the truth of the promised reward. But to whom? to those who walk in innocence.
*O Lord of hosts, blessed is the man that hopeth,* etc. Thou who dost such great things, which cannot be told.

notes.text: Brethren — This is the only place in this epistle where he uses this compellation. Soldiers frequently use it to each other in the field. Be strong - Nothing less will suffice for such a fight: to be weak, and remain so, is the way to perish. In the power of his might - A very uncommon expression, plainly denoting what great assistance we need as if his might would not do, it must be the powerful exertion of his might.

Put on the whole armour of God — The Greek word means a complete suit of armour. Believers are said to put on the girdle, breastplate, shoes; to take the shield of faith, and sword of the Spirit. The whole armour - As if the armour would scarce do, it must be the whole armour. This is repeated, ver. 13, because of the strength and subtilty of our adversaries, and because of an "evil day" of sore trial being at hand.

For our wrestling is not only, not chiefly, against flesh and blood — Weak men, or fleshly appetites. But against principalities, against powers - The mighty princes of all the infernal legions. And great is their power, and that likewise of those legions whom they command. Against the rulers of the world - Perhaps these principalities and powers remain mostly in the citadel of their kingdom of darkness. But there are other evil spirits who range abroad, to whom the provinces of the world are committed. Of the darkness - This is chiefly spiritual darkness. Of this age - Which prevails during the present state of things. Against wicked spirits - Who continually oppose faith, love, holiness, either by force or fraud; and labour to infuse unbelief, pride, idolatry malice, envy, anger, hatred. In heavenly places - Which were once their abode, and which they still aspire to, as far as they are permitted.

In the evil day — The war is perpetual; but the fight is one day less, another more, violent. The evil day is either at the approach of death, or in life; may be longer or shorter and admits of numberless varieties. And having done all, to stand - That ye may still keep on your armour, still stand upon your guard, still watch and pray; and thus ye will be enabled to endure unto the end, and stand with joy before the face of the Son of Man.

Having your loins girt about — That ye may be ready for every motion. With truth - Not only with the truths of the gospel, but with "truth in the inward parts;" for without this all our knowledge of divine truth will prove but a poor girdle "in the evil day." So our Lord is described, Isaiah xi, 5. And as a girded man is always ready to go on, so this seems to intimate an obedient heart, a ready will. Our Lord adds to the loins girded, the lights burning, Luke xii, 35; showing that watching and ready obedience are the inseparable companions of faith and love. And having on the breastplate of righteousness - The righteousness of a spotless purity, in which Christ will present us faultless before God, through the merit of his own blood. With this breastplate our Lord is described, Isaiah lix, 17. In the breast is the seat of conscience, which is guarded by righteousness. No armour for the back is mentioned. We are always to face our enemies.

And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel — Let this be always ready to direct and confirm you in every step. This part of the armour, for the feet, is needful, considering what a journey we have to go; what a race to run. Our feet must be so shod, that our footsteps slip not. To order our life and conversation aright, we are prepared by the gospel blessing, the peace and love of God ruling in the heart, Colossians iii, 14, 15. By this only can we tread the rough ways, surmount our difficulties, and hold out to the end.

Above or over all — As a sort of universal covering to every other part of the armour itself, continually exercise a strong and lively faith. This you may use as a shield, which will quench all the fiery darts, the furious temptations, violent and sudden injections of the devil.

And take for an helmet the hope of salvation — 1 Thess. v, 8. The head is that part which is most carefully to be defended. One stroke here may prove fatal. The armour for this is the hope of salvation. The lowest degree of this hope is a confidence that God will work the whole work of faith in us; the highest is a full assurance of future glory, added to the experimental knowledge of pardoning love. Armed with this helmet, the hope of the joy set before him, Christ "endured the cross, and despised the shame," Heb. xii, 2. And the sword of the Spirit, the word of God - This Satan cannot withstand, when it is edged and wielded by faith. Till now our armour has been only defensive. But we are to attack Satan, as well as secure ourselves; the shield in one hand, and the sword in the other. Whoever fights with the powers of hell will need both. He that is covered with armour from head to foot, and neglects this, will be foiled after all. This whole description shows us how great a thing it is to be a Christian. The want of any one thing makes him incomplete. Though he has his loins girt with truth, righteousness for a breastplate, his feet shod with the preparation of the gospel, the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit; yet one thing he wants after all. What is that? It follows,

Praying always — At all times, and on every occasion, in midst of all employments, inwardly praying without ceasing. By the Spirit - Through the influence of the Holy Spirit. With all prayer - With all sort of prayer, public, private, mental, vocal. Some are careful in respect of one kind of prayer, and negligent in others. If we would have the petitions we ask, let us use all. Some there are who use only mental prayer or ejaculations, and think they are in a state of grace, and use a way of worship, far superior to any other: but such only fancy themselves to be above what is really above them; it requiring far more grace to be enabled to pour out a fervent and continued prayer, than to offer up mental aspirations. And supplication - Repeating and urging our prayer, as Christ did in the garden. And watching - Inwardly attending on God, to know his will, to gain power to do it, and to attain to the blessings we desire. With all perseverance - Continuing to the end in this holy exercise. And supplication for all the saints - Wrestling in fervent, continued intercession for others, especially for the faithful, that they may do all the will of God, and be steadfast to the end. Perhaps we receive few answers to prayer, because we do not intercede enough for others.
By the opening my mouth — Removing every inward and every outward hindrance.
An ambassador in bonds — The ambassadors of men usually appear in great pomp. How differently does the ambassador of Christ appear!

glossa.text: *For the rest.* After the special precepts by which he admonished the several orders, now he admonishes all in common; as if: Thus far I have helped you by word and by work; henceforth, in the time to come, in the remaining time, by faith and by love.

*Rulers of the world.* They are not so called for this reason, that they rule the world, which consists of heaven and earth; but he calls sinners the world, concerning which John: *And the world knew him not ((Joan. I))*. Such a world do they rule, against whom we have perpetual enmities: because even that we suffer importunate men, they cause. For they instigate and inflame them, and move them as their own vessels, and touch them as instruments. Against them we have a hidden wrestling, for which the Apostle arms us. *Of darkness.* Lest the demons be thought to rule this visible world, he subjoins what he understood by the name of the world: *Of these darknesses,* that is, of sins; as if: The demons have dominion not over the world which consists of heaven and earth, but over sinners. *Against the spiritual things.* As if: The enemies are to be feared because they are spiritual and invisible, and because they are wicked: and they fight not for a small matter, but for the taking away of the heavenly inheritance. As heavenly things he calls the virtues, in which we suffer the battle of the demons, or the wicked spirits are in the heavenly places, that is, in this lower air. For they, as horsemen, fight upon men as horses. Let us then slay the horsemen, let us possess the horses.

*Having your loins girt,* etc. That is, bridling carnal concupiscences with the girdle of chastity, not feignedly, but in truth, or through charity. *Having put on the breastplate of justice.* Rightly is the breastplate compared to justice, because, as a breastplate is woven of many rings, so justice consists of many virtues. Otherwise: Justice can be compared to a breastplate because, as a breastplate fortifies the breast, binds the belly, protects the thighs, so justice repels the superfluous thoughts which are wont to turn about in the breast: it binds the gluttony of the belly, and represses lust also.

*Shod.* Mark says that the apostles were shod with sandals, or with soles, so that the foot should neither be straight *rectus*; read *tectus*, "covered", nor bare to the ground, that is, that the Gospel should neither be hidden, nor lean upon earthly advantages. *The feet.* That is, let the affections be fortified with virtues, lest they be pricked by vices, so that they may thus be ready to preach the Gospel which announces peace between God and man; or that they may be ready to fulfil the precepts of the Gospel.
*The shield of faith.* Faith is a shield, under which justice is safe, as under the defence of all the virtues, which is stretched before all arms and which the devil assails first of all.

*And the helmet.* The helmet is eternal salvation, the memory of which enwraps the mind lest it fail. *And the sword of the spirit.* The word of God is a twice-sharpened sword, teaching concerning things temporal and eternal. Promising the consolation of the former in the Old, the perfection of the latter in the New Testament. For what has been promised to us temporally, [belongs] to the one part of the sword: but what is unto everlasting belongs to the other part of the sword. For therefore also they are called two Testaments, because the Old promises earthly things, the New eternal. Concerning this sword the Lord says: *I came not to send peace upon the earth, but the sword ((Matth. X))* . This sword is truly sharp, because it divides from the world him whom it has made.
*In the spirit.* He prays in the spirit who prays with a clean conscience and an entire faith. He prays in the flesh who with a polluted mind sins again, not by chance, but of set purpose.

*Unto the opening,* etc. That is, that I may be able openly to unlock the mystery of the Gospel, that is, the secrets of the incarnation and of the passion. As if: Lest the pressure of tribulation by very dread should blunt the edge of doctrine.

notes.text: I live by the Father — Being one with him. He shall live by me -Being one with me. Amazing union!
This is — That is, I am the bread - Which is not like the manna your fathers ate, who died notwithstanding.
This is a hard saying — Hard to the children of the world, but sweet to the children of God. Scarce ever did our Lord speak more sublimely, even to the apostles in private. Who can hear - Endure it?
What if ye shall see the Son of man ascend where he was before? — How much more incredible will it then appear to you, that he should give you his flesh to eat?

It is the Spirit — The spiritual meaning of these words, by which God giveth life. The flesh - The bare, carnal, literal meaning, profiteth nothing. The words which I have spoken, they are spirit - Are to be taken in a spiritual sense and, when they are so understood, they are life - That is, a means of spiritual life to the hearers.

But there are some of you who believe not — And so receive no life by them, because you take them in a gross literal sense. For Jesus knew from the beginning - Of his ministry: who would betray him - Therefore it is plain, God does foresee future contingencies:- "But his foreknowledge causes not the fault, Which had no less proved certain unforeknown."
Unless it be given — And it is given to those only who will receive it on God's own terms.
From this time many of his disciples went back — So our Lord now began to purge his floor: the proud and careless were driven away, and those remained who were meet for the Master's use.
Thou hast the words of eternal life — Thou, and thou alone, speakest the words which show the way to life everlasting.
And we — Who have been with thee from the beginning, whatever others do, have known - Are absolutely assured, that thou art the Christ.

glossa.text: *For the flesh.* Truly the soul and the body shall live from this food, because *my flesh is meat indeed.* Which alone makes men immortal, so that they shall neither hunger nor thirst; another food does not afford this, even if this be sought in it.

*He that eateth.* Now he expounds how that comes to pass which he said, and what it is to eat the flesh and to drink the blood: that is, to abide in Christ and to have Christ abiding in oneself. But he who does not abide in Christ, and in whom Christ does not abide, does not eat spiritually, and so takes the sacrament to himself bodily unto judgment.

*As the Father hath sent me.* He sent me, equal to himself; that is, he made me man, and thence it is that I refer my life to him as to one greater. *And he shall live.* That I live by the Father, my own emptying-out effects; that a man live by me, the participation effects which eats me.

*This is the bread.* And so it is established that this is truly the bread from heaven, not the manna, because the fathers like to you who ate it are dead for ever: whereas the man who had not life, eating this bread, shall live for ever. Above he had said, *I am the bread that came down from heaven.* Here he says: This man, that is, the Son of man, to the eating of whose flesh I invite you, is that *bread which came down from heaven:* therefore the Son of man and the Son of God are the same.

*Many therefore.* Many, being wise after the flesh, as though he were promising that he would distribute to them, piece by piece, the flesh wherewith he was clothed, think it to be against nature that he should give human flesh as food for men.

 *This is a hard saying,* etc. ((AUG.)) So it behoved to be said, that it might not be understood by men, but that the secret of God might be covered with words: the secret of God ought to make men intent, not adverse.

*If then,* etc. The speech is left suspended. As if he should say: Then shall you understand that I do not give out my body in the manner you suppose, and that this grace is not consumed by bites, but that, by giving myself to them with a spiritual grace, I turn them into my body; hereby he plainly resolves what had moved them; for they thought that he would distribute his body, whereas he says that he is to ascend into heaven whole and entire. What therefore is to be held, he openly adds:

*It is the spirit that quickeneth.* The flesh, as you understand it, as that which is bought in the shambles, as any other food, profits nothing; yet that same flesh, the vessel of the spirit which works salvation in it, profits much: as knowledge alone puffs up, yet is not itself evil, but by charity builds up.

*The words that I,* etc. By which I said that I am to be eaten, that one abides in me and I in him. But that anyone should abide in Christ as a member, and Christ in him as in a temple, unity effects. And unity is from charity, and charity from the spirit; therefore the spirit which quickens does not separate the members joined together.

*But there are some,* etc. The prophet: Unless you believe, you shall not understand. By faith we are coupled, by understanding we are quickened.

*And who should betray.* Because Judas withdraws among those who were scandalized, but remains to lay snares; whom he neither passes over in silence nor openly points out, that all may fear while one perishes.
*Because no man can,* etc. He adds the cause why certain men do not believe: Because it is not given by God; for faith is not to men from themselves, as if their own, but from God, as a grace.

*From this,* etc. Note that one must speak warily; but if nevertheless someone shall be scandalized at thy words, he has consolation in him at whose saying many were scandalized, who did this that it might be an example to thee.

doctrine.article: on the third day he rose

notes.text:
All Israel — Namely, their representatives. Shechem - To the city of Shechem, a place convenient for the purpose, not only because it was a Levitical city, and a city of refuge, and a place near Joshua's city, but especially for the two main ends for which he summoned them thither.

1. For the solemn burial of the bones of Joseph, and the rest of the patriarchs, for which this place was designed.

2. For the solemn renewing of their covenant with God; which in this place was first made between God and Abraham, Gen. xii, 6, 7, and afterwards renewed by the Israelites at their first entrance into the land of Canaan, between the two mountains of Ebal and Gerizzim, chap. viii, 30, &c. which were very near Shechem: and therefore this place was most proper, both to remind them of their former obligations to God, and to engage them to a farther ratification of them. Before God - As in God's presence, to hear what Joshua was to speak to them in God's name, and to receive God's commands from his mouth. He had taken a solemn farewell before: but as God renewed his strength, he desired to improve it for their good. We must never think our work for God done, 'till our life is done.

The people — To the elders, by whom it was to be imparted to all the rest, and to as many of the people as came thither. He spake to them in God's name, and as from him, in the language of a prophet, Thus saith the Lord. Jehovah, the great God, and the God of Israel, whom you are peculiarly engaged to hear. The flood - Or, the river, namely, Euphrates, so called by way of eminency. They served - That is, Both Abraham and Nahor were no less idolaters than the rest of mankind. This is said to prevent their vain boasting in their worthy ancestors, and to assure them that whatsoever good was in, or had been done by their progenitors, was wholly from God's free grace, and not for their own merit or righteousness.
The face — His anger, which discovers itself in the face.

Nigh — Ready to hear and succor them. To - Those whose spirits are truly humbled under the hand of God, and the sense of their sins, whose hearts are subdued, and made obedient to God's will and submissive to his providence.

Bones — All the parts and members of their bodies. David prays for deliverance from his enemies, and prophecies their destruction, ver. 1-10, Describes their wickedness, ver. 11-21. Foretells their confusion, the joy of the righteous, and his own thanksgiving, ver. 22-28. A psalm of David.

glossa.text:
*The eyes of the Lord,* etc. ((ID.)) Of the retributions of the good and of the evil, lest in dangers the just man grow soft with any doubt.

*The eyes of the Lord.* Nor shouldst thou distrust out of thy weakness, because *the eyes.*

*Unto the prayers.* ((ID.)) The swiftness of hearing, since the hearer dwells in them.
*The memory.* ((AUG.)) That not even the mention, etc., *as far as* which they have committed.
*The Lord is nigh.* He delivered: for he is inclined to this, because *he is nigh;* or, there is an allusion to the crying out.

*Many are the tribulations of the just.* As also in the New Testament, *he is nigh, and he will save,* which is necessary, because *many are the tribulations.* ((CASS.)) *Many;* from the devil, from envious men, and from oneself. *He will deliver.* ((AUG.)) Not bodily, but by giving them patience: or, he will deliver spiritually.
*The bones.* ((ID.)) The virtues. *And one,* etc., that not even patience may perish.

*Most evil.* ((ID.)) Not merely evil, although it end amid riches and perfumes and the lamentations of men, yet it is most evil, because in sins it drags down to hell.

*That hate.* Whose? Not of all, because they are sinners; but of those who hate the just one, who justifies, that is, Christ, through whom he that is not reconciled perishes: but *he will redeem the souls,* in respect of which the death is most evil.

The lowest degree of this hope is a confidence that God will work the whole work of faith in us; the highest is a full assurance of future glory, added to the experimental knowledge of pardoning love. Armed with this helmet, the hope of the joy set before him, Christ "endured the cross, and despised the shame," Heb. xii, 2. And the sword of the Spirit, the word of God - This Satan cannot withstand, when it is edged and wielded by faith. Till now our armour has been only defensive. But we are to attack Satan, as well as secure ourselves; the shield in one hand, and the sword in the other. Whoever fights with the powers of hell will need both. He that is covered with armour from head to foot, and neglects this, will be foiled after all. This whole description shows us how great a thing it is to be a Christian. The want of any one thing makes him incomplete. Though he has his loins girt with truth, righteousness for a breastplate, his feet shod with the preparation of the gospel, the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit; yet one thing he wants after all. What is that? It follows,

Praying always — At all times, and on every occasion, in midst of all employments, inwardly praying without ceasing. By the Spirit - Through the influence of the Holy Spirit. With all prayer - With all sort of prayer, public, private, mental, vocal. Some are careful in respect of one kind of prayer, and negligent in others. If we would have the petitions we ask, let us use all. Some there are who use only mental prayer or ejaculations, and think they are in a state of grace, and use a way of worship, far superior to any other: but such only fancy themselves to be above what is really above them; it requiring far more grace to be enabled to pour out a fervent and continued prayer, than to offer up mental aspirations. And supplication - Repeating and urging our prayer, as Christ did in the garden. And watching - Inwardly attending on God, to know his will, to gain power to do it, and to attain to the blessings we desire. With all perseverance - Continuing to the end in this holy exercise. And supplication for all the saints - Wrestling in fervent, continued intercession for others, especially for the faithful, that they may do all the will of God, and be steadfast to the end. Perhaps we receive few answers to prayer, because we do not intercede enough for others.
By the opening my mouth — Removing every inward and every outward hindrance.
An ambassador in bonds — The ambassadors of men usually appear in great pomp. How differently does the ambassador of Christ appear!

glossa.text: *For the rest.* After the special precepts by which he admonished the several orders, now he admonishes all in common; as if: Thus far I have helped you by word and by work; henceforth, in the time to come, in the remaining time, by faith and by love.

*Rulers of the world.* They are not so called for this reason, that they rule the world, which consists of heaven and earth; but he calls sinners the world, concerning which John: *And the world knew him not ((Joan. I))*. Such a world do they rule, against whom we have perpetual enmities: because even that we suffer importunate men, they cause. For they instigate and inflame them, and move them as their own vessels, and touch them as instruments. Against them we have a hidden wrestling, for which the Apostle arms us. *Of darkness.* Lest the demons be thought to rule this visible world, he subjoins what he understood by the name of the world: *Of these darknesses,* that is, of sins; as if: The demons have dominion not over the world which consists of heaven and earth, but over sinners. *Against the spiritual things.* As if: The enemies are to be feared because they are spiritual and invisible, and because they are wicked: and they fight not for a small matter, but for the taking away of the heavenly inheritance. As heavenly things he calls the virtues, in which we suffer the battle of the demons, or the wicked spirits are in the heavenly places, that is, in this lower air. For they, as horsemen, fight upon men as horses. Let us then slay the horsemen, let us possess the horses.

*Having your loins girt,* etc. That is, bridling carnal concupiscences with the girdle of chastity, not feignedly, but in truth, or through charity. *Having put on the breastplate of justice.* Rightly is the breastplate compared to justice, because, as a breastplate is woven of many rings, so justice consists of many virtues. Otherwise: Justice can be compared to a breastplate because, as a breastplate fortifies the breast, binds the belly, protects the thighs, so justice repels the superfluous thoughts which are wont to turn about in the breast: it binds the gluttony of the belly, and represses lust also.

*Shod.* Mark says that the apostles were shod with sandals, or with soles, so that the foot should neither be straight *rectus*; read *tectus*, "covered", nor bare to the ground, that is, that the Gospel should neither be hidden, nor lean upon earthly advantages. *The feet.* That is, let the affections be fortified with virtues, lest they be pricked by vices, so that they may thus be ready to preach the Gospel which announces peace between God and man; or that they may be ready to fulfil the precepts of the Gospel.
*The shield of faith.* Faith is a shield, under which justice is safe, as under the defence of all the virtues, which is stretched before all arms and which the devil assails first of all.

*And the helmet.* The helmet is eternal salvation, the memory of which enwraps the mind lest it fail. *And the sword of the spirit.* The word of God is a twice-sharpened sword, teaching concerning things temporal and eternal. Promising the consolation of the former in the Old, the perfection of the latter in the New Testament. For what has been promised to us temporally, [belongs] to the one part of the sword: but what is unto everlasting belongs to the other part of the sword. For therefore also they are called two Testaments, because the Old promises earthly things, the New eternal. Concerning this sword the Lord says: *I came not to send peace upon the earth, but the sword ((Matth. X))* . This sword is truly sharp, because it divides from the world him whom it has made.
*In the spirit.* He prays in the spirit who prays with a clean conscience and an entire faith. He prays in the flesh who with a polluted mind sins again, not by chance, but of set purpose.

*Unto the opening,* etc. That is, that I may be able openly to unlock the mystery of the Gospel, that is, the secrets of the incarnation and of the passion. As if: Lest the pressure of tribulation by very dread should blunt the edge of doctrine.

notes.text: I live by the Father — Being one with him. He shall live by me -Being one with me. Amazing union!
This is — That is, I am the bread - Which is not like the manna your fathers ate, who died notwithstanding.
This is a hard saying — Hard to the children of the world, but sweet to the children of God. Scarce ever did our Lord speak more sublimely, even to the apostles in private. Who can hear - Endure it?
What if ye shall see the Son of man ascend where he was before? — How much more incredible will it then appear to you, that he should give you his flesh to eat?

It is the Spirit — The spiritual meaning of these words, by which God giveth life. The flesh - The bare, carnal, literal meaning, profiteth nothing. The words which I have spoken, they are spirit - Are to be taken in a spiritual sense and, when they are so understood, they are life - That is, a means of spiritual life to the hearers.

But there are some of you who believe not — And so receive no life by them, because you take them in a gross literal sense. For Jesus knew from the beginning - Of his ministry: who would betray him - Therefore it is plain, God does foresee future contingencies:- "But his foreknowledge causes not the fault, Which had no less proved certain unforeknown."
Unless it be given — And it is given to those only who will receive it on God's own terms.
From this time many of his disciples went back — So our Lord now began to purge his floor: the proud and careless were driven away, and those remained who were meet for the Master's use.
Thou hast the words of eternal life — Thou, and thou alone, speakest the words which show the way to life everlasting.
And we — Who have been with thee from the beginning, whatever others do, have known - Are absolutely assured, that thou art the Christ.

glossa.text: *For the flesh.* Truly the soul and the body shall live from this food, because *my flesh is meat indeed.* Which alone makes men immortal, so that they shall neither hunger nor thirst; another food does not afford this, even if this be sought in it.

*He that eateth.* Now he expounds how that comes to pass which he said, and what it is to eat the flesh and to drink the blood: that is, to abide in Christ and to have Christ abiding in oneself. But he who does not abide in Christ, and in whom Christ does not abide, does not eat spiritually, and so takes the sacrament to himself bodily unto judgment.

*As the Father hath sent me.* He sent me, equal to himself; that is, he made me man, and thence it is that I refer my life to him as to one greater. *And he shall live.* That I live by the Father, my own emptying-out effects; that a man live by me, the participation effects which eats me.

*This is the bread.* And so it is established that this is truly the bread from heaven, not the manna, because the fathers like to you who ate it are dead for ever: whereas the man who had not life, eating this bread, shall live for ever. Above he had said, *I am the bread that came down from heaven.* Here he says: This man, that is, the Son of man, to the eating of whose flesh I invite you, is that *bread which came down from heaven:* therefore the Son of man and the Son of God are the same.

*Many therefore.* Many, being wise after the flesh, as though he were promising that he would distribute to them, piece by piece, the flesh wherewith he was clothed, think it to be against nature that he should give human flesh as food for men.

 *This is a hard saying,* etc. ((AUG.)) So it behoved to be said, that it might not be understood by men, but that the secret of God might be covered with words: the secret of God ought to make men intent, not adverse.

*If then,* etc. The speech is left suspended. As if he should say: Then shall you understand that I do not give out my body in the manner you suppose, and that this grace is not consumed by bites, but that, by giving myself to them with a spiritual grace, I turn them into my body; hereby he plainly resolves what had moved them; for they thought that he would distribute his body, whereas he says that he is to ascend into heaven whole and entire. What therefore is to be held, he openly adds:

*It is the spirit that quickeneth.* The flesh, as you understand it, as that which is bought in the shambles, as any other food, profits nothing; yet that same flesh, the vessel of the spirit which works salvation in it, profits much: as knowledge alone puffs up, yet is not itself evil, but by charity builds up.

*The words that I,* etc. By which I said that I am to be eaten, that one abides in me and I in him. But that anyone should abide in Christ as a member, and Christ in him as in a temple, unity effects. And unity is from charity, and charity from the spirit; therefore the spirit which quickens does not separate the members joined together.

*But there are some,* etc. The prophet: Unless you believe, you shall not understand. By faith we are coupled, by understanding we are quickened.

*And who should betray.* Because Judas withdraws among those who were scandalized, but remains to lay snares; whom he neither passes over in silence nor openly points out, that all may fear while one perishes.
*Because no man can,* etc. He adds the cause why certain men do not believe: Because it is not given by God; for faith is not to men from themselves, as if their own, but from God, as a grace.

*From this,* etc. Note that one must speak warily; but if nevertheless someone shall be scandalized at thy words, he has consolation in him at whose saying many were scandalized, who did this that it might be an example to thee.

registers.label: Spare
lines: How lovely is your dwelling place, O Lord of hosts.
Our souls long for the courts of the living God.
This teaching is hard; many turned and walked away.
But Lord, to whom shall we go?
Will God really dwell on the earth with us?
Heaven cannot hold you, yet you meet us here.
You have the words of eternal life; come, let us worship.
We have come, and we will stay. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: How lovely is your dwelling place; even the sparrow finds a home and the swallow a nest near your altar, O Lord of hosts.
Give us this bread always.
Solomon stood in the finished temple and wondered aloud: will God truly dwell on earth, when heaven itself cannot contain you?
Give us this bread always.
The teaching was hard, and many who had followed turned back and walked with him no more; he asked the twelve, will you also go?
Give us this bread always.
And Peter answered for all of us: Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life; so here we are, and here we stay.
Give us this bread always. You have the words of eternal life.
